# Kestrel

> Load testing for Kotlin. A scenario is an ordinary Kotlin value, and the run
> times every request from the moment it was *meant* to depart — so the tail it
> reports is the target's, not a queue the generator made. Every run states
> whether the generator kept its own schedule, so one that fell behind is not
> quietly green. No base class, no registration, no XML, no container: a load
> test is an ordinary JUnit 5 or Kotest test.

Facts worth having before anything else:

- Kotlin 2.4, JVM 21+, Apache 2.0. Virtual threads on the JDK's own HTTP client.
- Nothing is on Maven Central yet; `./gradlew publishToMavenLocal` is how to get
  it today. Coordinates are `io.github.matthewjones372:kestrel-core` and its
  siblings — `kestrel-http`, `kestrel-junit5`, `kestrel-report-html` and the rest
  under Docs below. `kestrel-core` depends on the Kotlin standard library and
  nothing else, and a test enforces it; every client, broker, test framework and
  report format is a leaf module beside it.
- A step is named once. `step("place order")` gives a `StepName`, and the same
  handle indexes the result — `result[placeOrder]` — so a rename is a compile
  error rather than an assertion about a step nobody runs. Session values are
  named the same way: `sessionKey<String>("orderId")` goes in through `capture`
  and comes back out of `get` as a `String`.
- Checks belong on the request — `expecting(201)`, `checking("has an id") { }` —
  and a failed step is counted rather than thrown, with the `Reason` that failed
  it: `result[placeOrder].failed.count`, `failedWith(HttpStatus(503))`.
- A step that is not one request is a body — `exec(pay) { send(...) }` — and what
  you call in it is timed like any other step. A simulation is a value, so
  `checkout.at(50.perSecond, over = 1.minutes).userCount()` answers before it runs.

## The shape of a test

`@LoadTest` is `@Test` with a `Kestrel` parameter, here against a JDK `HttpServer`.

```kotlin
import io.github.matthewjones372.kestrel.at
import io.github.matthewjones372.kestrel.engine.Kestrel
import io.github.matthewjones372.kestrel.fedBy
import io.github.matthewjones372.kestrel.feed
import io.github.matthewjones372.kestrel.http.http
import io.github.matthewjones372.kestrel.junit5.LoadTest
import io.github.matthewjones372.kestrel.perSecond
import io.github.matthewjones372.kestrel.scenario
import io.github.matthewjones372.kestrel.sessionKey
import io.github.matthewjones372.kestrel.step
import io.kotest.matchers.shouldBe
import kotlin.time.Duration.Companion.seconds

private val orderId = sessionKey<String>("orderId")
private val customer = sessionKey<String>("customer")

private val browse = step("browse")
private val placeOrder = step("place order")

class CheckoutLoadTest {

    @LoadTest
    fun `checkout holds up at fifty a second`(kestrel: Kestrel) {
        val api = http.baseUrl("http://localhost:${server.address.port}")

        val checkout = scenario("checkout") {
            exec(browse, api.get("/products/{customer}"))
            exec(
                placeOrder,
                api.post("/orders")
                    .body("""{"cart":"1 anvil"}""")
                    .expecting(201)
                    .capture(orderId) { response -> response.header("location") },
            )
        }

        val result = kestrel.run(
            checkout.at(50.perSecond, over = 1.seconds)
                .fedBy(feed(customer) { user -> "customer-$user" }),
        )

        result[browse].count shouldBe 50L
        result[placeOrder].failed.count shouldBe 0L
    }
}
```

## What it will not do

- No `Thread.sleep` in library code: pacing is scheduled, not parked, and detekt
  fails the build on it. Think time is `pause(200.milliseconds)` in the scenario.
- No smoothing and no interpolation: a percentile is the top of the bucket a
  sample landed in, and a number on a report was measured or it is not there.
- No registry, nothing to run at startup, and no `main` of its own.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/matthewjones372/kestrel/blob/main/README.md): what it is, and the smallest test that runs.
- [Cookbook](https://github.com/matthewjones372/kestrel/blob/main/docs/cookbook.md):
  profiles, feeders, captures, goals, gRPC, Kafka, JDBC, WebSockets, baselines and reports. Start here for code.
- [Modules](https://github.com/matthewjones372/kestrel/blob/main/docs/modules.md): each module, and what it depends on.
- [What it costs](https://github.com/matthewjones372/kestrel/blob/main/docs/what-it-costs.md): the tool's own measured overhead.
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/matthewjones372/kestrel/blob/main/AGENTS.md): for working *on* Kestrel, not with it.
